newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares to take lead from gold next week.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares to take lead from gold next week.

text.p: South African shares should take direction from a variety of sources next week although much of the market's attention will remain focused on gold, dealers and portfolio managers said on Friday.
Other factors expected to determine the market's mood were the weaker rand and local bonds, stronger international bourses and latest trade data, they said.

"It will depend on how the gold price behaves. If the weaker rand, gold price and bonds continue...the market will probably go weak," Johan Marais, director at Societe General Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.

After recently touching fresh 12-year lows, gold struggled to keep its head above the $320 level this week. The metal's woes have raised fears among local economists about the impact it will have on marginal mines as well as the country's balance of payments.
Portfolio managers said that while the gold price would remain volatile, it was likely to trade in a range of between $318 and $325 per ounce in the short-term.
"July and August is a vulnerable period for gold shares. I do not see bullion roaring ahead. It will hold between $325 and 318," Tom Bramwell-Jones, portfolio manager at EW Balderson, said.

Traders said concern about the local bond and currency would also linger next week. Bond yields have hovered around the 14.30 percent level following a retracement from 17-month lows posted earlier in the month, while the rand probed its weakest level in six months on Friday when it traded around the 4.56 level.
Wall Street and the FTSE would also bolster local shares next week if their strength was sustained, as would continuing hopes for a cut in local interest rates later in the year.
"The market will be driven on sentiment on the FTSE and the Dow...There are expectations that there might be a rate cut in September," said Investec international trader Dominic Rey.
Both the U.S. and British stock markets rallied to fresh highs during the week.
Traders said the market could take further direction from June trade data, possibly due for release in the latter half of next week.
Economists polled by Reuters on average forecast a surplus of 1.28 billion for June from a 1.75 billion surplus in May. Estimates ranged between 800 million rand 1.8 billion rand.
Company results due next week include hotels to building firm Stocks & Stocks Ltd's year results and drinks and sweets firm Cadbury Schweppes (South Africa) Ltd's interim results.

Steep finance charges, a much higher tax payment and a tough real estate market were expected to weigh down year earnings at Stock and Stocks Ltd but Cadswep was set to post healthy half year growth buoyed by good local demand and a windfall from a stake in Amalgamated Beverage Industries Ltd (ABI) . -- Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482 1003
